kind: Public, authored read-only demonstration; real document quotes, no live model/search result claimed
claim: Python requires every line to contain at most 79 characters.

sources.title: PEP 8 — Python style guidance
sources.quote: Limit all lines to a maximum of 79 characters.
sources.scope: PEP 8 also allows an agreeing team to choose longer code lines, up to 99. The standard library follows the more conservative limit.

sources.title: Black — formatter default
sources.quote: Black defaults to 88 characters per line
sources.scope: This is a configurable formatter default, not a universal Python language requirement. It does not establish that one line length improves every project.

assessment: The claim is too broad. PEP 8 gives style guidance with a team exception; Black uses a different configurable default. Neither document makes 79 a language-wide requirement.
unknown: This example does not measure developer productivity, prove author identity, or establish independent scientific corroboration.
